content: 1. Tisagenlecleucel and ustekinumab both enhance each other's immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 2. Tocilizumab and ustekinumab both increase immunosuppressive effects, leading to a higher risk of infection. Avoid this combination or consider alternative therapies. 3. Ustekinumab and Tongkat Ali both enhance immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 4. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of inactivated vaccines for traveler’s diarrhea and cholera due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 5. Immunosuppressants, including ustekinumab, increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. Patients should receive all age-appropriate immunizations as per current guidelines before initiating therapy. 6. Ustekinumab decreases the efficacy of the typhoid polysaccharide vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Ustekinumab reduces the effectiveness of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Ustekinumab decreases the efficacy of the varicella virus live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Ustekinumab reduces the effectiveness of the yellow fever vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Ustekinumab decreases the efficacy of the zoster live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Ustekinumab may alter the metabolism of drugs like alfentanil by normalizing CYP450 enzyme formation, which can be affected by chronic inflammation. Monitor therapeutic effects when initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients on CYP450 substrates. 12. Ustekinumab may interact with amphotericin B cholesteryl sulfate by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 13. Ustekinumab may interact with amphotericin B deoxycholate by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 14. Ustekinumab increases immunosuppressive effects, while astragalus decreases them. The interaction effect is unclear, so use caution and monitor closely. 15. Belatacept and ustekinumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Ustekinumab may interact with carbamazepine by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 17. Ustekinumab may interact with clonidine by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 18. Ustekinumab may interact with colchicine by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 19. Ustekinumab may interact with cyclosporine by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 20. Ustekinumab may interact with denosumab, increasing the risk of serious infections in immunosuppressed patients. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Ustekinumab may interact with digoxin by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 22. Ustekinumab may interact with dihydroergotamine by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 23. Ustekinumab may interact with disopyramide by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 24. Ustekinumab may interact with divalproex sodium by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 25. Ustekinumab increases immunosuppressive effects, while echinacea decreases them. The interaction effect is unclear, so use caution and monitor closely. 26. Efgartigimod alfa may reduce ustekinumab’s effectiveness by receptor binding competition. Monitor for reduced efficacy and consider alternative therapies if long-term use is necessary. 27. Efgartigimod/hyaluronidase may reduce ustekinumab’s effectiveness by receptor binding competition. Monitor for reduced efficacy and consider alternative therapies if long-term use is necessary. 28. Ustekinumab may interact with ergotamine by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 29. Ustekinumab may interact with ethosuximide by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 30. Ustekinumab may interact with everolimus by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 31. Ustekinumab may interact with fentanyl by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 32. Ustekinumab increases the immunosuppressive effects of fingolimod, raising the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 33. Ustekinumab may interact with fosphenytoin by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 34. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the Haemophilus influenzae type b vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid vaccination during immunosuppressive therapy if possible, and revaccinate after therapy is discontinued. 35. Ustekinumab decreases the efficacy of the inactivated hepatitis A vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis A/B vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Ustekinumab decreases the efficacy of the hepatitis A/typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Ustekinumab reduces the efficacy of the human papillomavirus (nonavalent) vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Hydroxyurea and ustekinumab may increase the risk of infection when used together. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Ifosfamide and ustekinumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Ustekinumab may interact with irinotecan by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 42. Ustekinumab and isavuconazonium sulfate both decrease immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Ustekinumab may interact with levothyroxine by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 44. Ustekinumab may interact with lithium by altering CYP450 enzyme formation. Use caution and monitor therapeutic effects. 45. Lomustine and ustekinumab both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely.
